name: BNN-27

lead: BNN-27 is a lab-made steroid-like molecule meant to imitate nerve growth factor (NGF). People in research-chemical circles discuss it for nerve and brain protection.

It is a DHEA analogue reported to bind the NGF receptors TrkA and p75NTR with high affinity, cross the blood-brain barrier and lack DHEA's hormonal activity. In mouse models it showed neuroprotective and neurogenic effects. Research is preclinical, with no human trials and no appearance use documented.

paras: It is discussed in nootropic and longevity circles as an NGF mimetic. No established human routine or timeline exists.
Human safety is unknown. It is not an approved drug.

angle.text: BNN-27 is a DHEA-derived NGF mimetic that its developers describe as lacking hormonal activity, and it is discussed for nerve and brain protection. No appearance use is documented; the research is preclinical.

lead: BNN-27 (17alpha,20R-epoxypregn-5-ene-3beta,21-diol) is a synthetic neurosteroid analogue of DHEA described as a "microneurotrophin" and an NGF mimetic. [1] It is reported to be a selective, high-affinity agonist of the TrkA and p75NTR receptors, to cross the blood-brain barrier, and to lack hormonal activity. [1]

It appears in longevity and brain-health discussions as a research compound for nerve protection and cognition, which people connect to staying sharp and healthy-looking as they age. Published work is in cells and animals: studies describe neuroprotective effects in mouse and rat models of Alzheimer's disease, spinal cord injury, retinal and optic nerve injury and diabetic retinopathy. [2][3][4][5] It has no approved use and no studied effect on appearance.

paras: Spiro derivatives of DHEA were first synthesized and assessed in 2009 as potential neuroprotective agents; BNN-27 was reported in 2016 to bind and activate TrkA and p75NTR. [1] Reviews of DHEA and its metabolites discuss this line of research. [6]

A 2025 study in Molecular Psychiatry examined BNN27 in the 5xFAD mouse model of Alzheimer's disease and linked reduced pathology to cognitive performance.[2] A 2023 study reported that BNN27 reduced astrogliosis and increased neuron density in a mouse spinal cord crush model.[3] A 2025 study reported anti-inflammatory and analgesic effects in a mouse inflammatory pain model.[4]

In rats, BNN27 counteracted ketamine-induced recognition memory deficits,[5] and a 2020 psychopharmacology study found no anxiolytic or antidepressant effects with its design.[7] Pharmacokinetic work in rodents describes rapid systemic elimination after a single injection.[8]
No studies found in humans. Reported work is in cells and rodents.[2][3][4][5]
